articles.title: Council Votes on Seasonal Farmers Market After Long Debate
articles.deck: Residents of Lower Millrace filled the hall on Thursday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Cyrus Hobart, who has lived in Lower Millrace for 18 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
The group has raised $12,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The Lower Millrace Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Thursday mornings. Public works estimates the work will take about 18 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Tannery Flats Gets $7,500 for Book Exchange Box
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in October.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 35 weeks once it begins. The group has raised $7,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

The Tannery Flats Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library. Karl Eckhart, who has lived in Tannery Flats for 35 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Saturday mornings. The plan calls for book exchange box along Rail Road, with work expected to start in October.

articles.title: Council Approves $850 for Nash Street Repairs
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Nash Street disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Councilmember Ida Cifuentes asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $850. Public works estimates the work will take about 15 weeks once it starts in November.
Residents of Stonebridge said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

articles.title: Stonebridge Garden Club Adds Community Oven
articles.deck: Residents of Stonebridge met on Sunday to talk over the plan.
body: The effort began in August when a handful of neighbors met at the Foundry Row fire house to talk about community oven. Several residents on Whitney Avenue said they had been waiting since 1977 for something like this.
The Stonebridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

articles.deck: The program begins in February and is open to all students in grade 3 and up.
body: Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for February.

articles.title: Letter: Support the Book Exchange Box
body: To the editor: I have lived on Union Avenue for 25 years, and I want to say what a difference the Cedar Hollow Garden Club has made. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

articles.title: Plans for Pet Adoption Fair Set for Eastgate This Summer
articles.deck: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public.
body: The event will be held at the Mill Hill town hall, rain or shine, with a backup date set for the following Sunday.

Children are welcome, and volunteers will be on hand to help with parking and set-up. Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public. Organizers ask guests to bring a dish to share or a little cash for supplies.

Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Kettle Hill Park gate on Saturday at 7 p.m.

articles.title: Council Splits 4–3 on Seasonal Farmers Market
articles.deck: The vote came after 27 residents spoke at Wednesday’s session.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 27 weeks once it starts in December.
Councilmember Owen Pelletier asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $7,500.

Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.

articles.title: Letter: Support the Book Exchange Box
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the July meeting. Please keep the book exchange box in the budget. Many of us on Dayton Road use it every week.

articles.title: Patrice Sandoval, 95, Church Organist
articles.deck: Friends remember Patrice Sandoval for the many years of service to Hickory Ridge.
body: Patrice Sandoval died in October at home on Hickory Ridge Road, at the age of 95. Born in Hickory Ridge in the years after the war, Patrice Sandoval spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to Scout Troop 14 in his or her name.
